rows.etymology: 140. Rp. sidum (in village Maṇa sistum) ‘garlic; name of a sweet, red fruit’ (Zoller 1983), sidum ‘garlic’ (S. R. Sharma). This is perhaps a TB-AA hybrid compound with - dum ‘edible plant’ (Zoller 1983) which has a parallel in Byangsi and Chaudangsi dəm ‘garlic’, and here probably also Ks. thuum ‘garlic’ and Jaṭ. thom ‘garlic’ (Jukes [1987: 95]); si(s)- may be related with #5494 PTB *swa-n ‘onion; garlic’. The following suggested AA parallels seem to be comparable compounds or prefixed forms built with reflexes related to Proto-South Bahnaric *diəm ‘onion’: Mnong diem tɔːj ‘garlic’ (cf. Tampuan tɔɔj ‘resemble’) and Brao kədiam ‘garlic’, Kui derived (kh)thìːm ‘onion, garlic’, Surin Khmer ktim-sɑː ‘garlic’, Tˈin tiam ‘garlic’, Chong ktiəm ‘garlic’, Thavung kathîam ‘garlic’.
